query: The Snail Post {A snail is crossing the garden wall with a folded scrap of paper tucked under its shell. Maud's garden, it seems, has a postal service.|The snail post again. Three snails today, each with a note, all heading in different directions.|Snail post. You know the route now, along the wall and round the pear, about a day each way.} {The note within reach says "for whoever's next".|One note has been answered in a different hand.|{season == "winter": The snails are sluggish with cold, the notes damp.|The snail nearest you is wearing a dewdrop like a hat.}} Write a note and send it on {You write something kind for a stranger and tuck it under a shell. The snail sets off, at snail speed, with your secret.|You answer a note left by someone you'll never meet. It feels like talking across a very slow, very gentle river.|You write back to whoever's been writing. The snail takes the note, and an age, and you don't mind.} Read the notes on the way {You ease a note out from under a shell. It's a confession about a stolen apple, decades old. You put it back, a little ashamed.|You read three notes before the snails notice. One of them is about someone exactly like you.|You read the snail post like a gossip column. The snails take it personally; one refuses to move till you leave.}
